service.name: image-tools
service.description: Local-first image toolbox: deterministic editing, on-demand AI generation/enhancement, and image analysis via CLI, UI, and API.

openrouter.description: Optional BYOK cloud image backend (last tier). The concrete model is resolved per request from an OpenRouter policy role; callers carry intent via the openrouter_role param.

device-studio.degraded_behavior: Image operations and preparation review remain available; scene import reports Device Studio unavailable until that owner recovers.
device-studio.description: Optional conversion of reviewed photographic preparations into Device Studio scene candidates.

ai-gateway.description: Optional cloud-provider routing; local model operations do not require gateway availability.
ai-gateway.degraded_behavior: Local models and retained assets remain available; gateway-backed provider routes report their unavailable state.

database.rationale: Scenario-owned SQLite database contains durable job, model-install, adapter-install, settings, and audit state; whole-file cleanup is forbidden.

budget.rationale: Durable application state is alarm-only; reclaim requires domain migrations or explicit database maintenance.

models.rationale: Downloaded model weights are expensive, user-selected durable assets and are never candidates for blob-output cleanup.

budget.rationale: Observed model weights are approximately 88GiB; the ceiling allows catalog growth while surfacing runaway downloads without authorizing deletion.

adapters.rationale: Downloaded conditioning adapters are durable selected assets and are protected from retention cleanup.

budget.rationale: Observed adapters are approximately 8GiB; the ceiling bounds future growth without permitting automatic deletion.

input_blobs.rationale: Uploaded source images are user-owned inputs and are not reproducible or cleanup candidates.

budget.rationale: Input retention is durable user work; the ceiling is alarm-only.

conditioning_blobs.rationale: Conditioning images are user-provided operation inputs and remain protected.

budget.rationale: Conditioning assets are durable inputs; the ceiling is alarm-only.

auxiliary_blobs.rationale: Mask and auxiliary blobs can be referenced by user operations and are protected from generic retention.

budget.rationale: Auxiliary operation inputs are alarm-only until their ownership model is explicit.

job_outputs.rationale: Managed output blobs are derived from terminal jobs. The image-tools owner retention loop (internal/cleanup/retention.go, every 30m) deletes outputs whose newest referencing job finished beyond max_age, then the oldest beyond max_bytes after a 1h grace; it protects pinned results, inputs of queued/running jobs, and files no successful job indexes, and writes the shared enforcement receipt plus retention/job-outputs-cycle.json with protected counts by reason. The storage-manager owner provider remains a reviewed, operator-approved path over the same eligibility. The writer uses the resolver-selected cache root; source images and retained preparation bundles remain in data.

budget.rationale: Thirty days preserves result retrieval for consumers that fetch late while bounding derived output growth (an August 2026 burst wrote 8.4k outputs, ~5GiB, never reclaimed). Consumers that keep a result must copy its bytes or pin the job; IMAGE_TOOLS_OUTPUT_RETENTION_MAX_AGE/_MAX_BYTES override for an operator.

python_runtime.rationale: The private Python environment is lock-rebuilt runtime material, separate from model weights and user data. The writer uses the resolver-selected cache root; source images and retained preparation bundles remain in data.

budget.rationale: The environment is rebuilt from the committed lock; the ceiling detects failed or duplicated provisioning. No age bound and no generic pruner: a live environment's files never change, so an age pruner selects every top-level entry (lib, bin, pyvenv.cfg) and leaves a half-deleted runtime.

sidecar_runtime.rationale: The embedded Python sidecar is materialized runtime code and can be rebuilt from source. The writer uses the resolver-selected cache root; source images and retained preparation bundles remain in data.

budget.rationale: Sidecar materialization is small and reproducible; the ceiling catches duplicate copies without authorizing active-runtime deletion. No age bound and no generic pruner: unchanging live runtime code would otherwise age into deletion.

deployment_state.rationale: Deployment reports are operational state retained for diagnostics and are not owned by job-output cleanup. The lifecycle writes this report below the resolver-selected data root.

budget.rationale: Deployment state is small and alarm-only.

diff_blobs.rationale: Comparison heatmaps are retained job results. Original comparison uploads are not retained, so exact reconstruction is not guaranteed and generic cleanup is forbidden.

budget.rationale: Measured 12KiB allocated on 2026-10-22; alarm-only ceiling covers comparison history without authorizing deletion.

database_wal.rationale: Live SQLite sidecar belongs to the durable database and must not be pruned independently.

budget.rationale: Alarm-only database sidecar budget; lifecycle/database ownership controls reconstruction and checkpointing.

database_shm.rationale: Live SQLite sidecar belongs to the durable database and must not be pruned independently.

budget.rationale: Alarm-only database sidecar budget; lifecycle/database ownership controls reconstruction and checkpointing.

scene_preparations.rationale: Immutable preparation revisions and review evidence survive disposable inference outputs; generic cleanup is forbidden.

budget.rationale: Alarm-only ceiling for retained photographic preparations; removal requires an owner retention policy.

scene_preparation_previews.rationale: Immutable preparation revisions and review evidence survive disposable inference outputs; generic cleanup is forbidden.

budget.rationale: Alarm-only ceiling for retained photographic preparations; removal requires an owner retention policy.

python_lock.rationale: Embedded dependency lock materialized beside the isolated cache runtime; canonical source remains committed.

budget.rationale: Alarm-only bound for the committed runtime lock.

legacy_python_runtime.rationale: Quiesced previous environment retained during cache-root migration, never executed; replacement is rebuilt through native lock-pinned provisioning.

budget.rationale: Temporary rollback retention; explicit cleanup after replacement qualification.

retention_receipts.rationale: Control-plane retention enforcement receipts retain operational audit state; not inference output or cleanup candidates.

budget.rationale: Alarm-only bound for the latest retention receipt.

storage.rationale: Image-tools declares each observed storage surface separately so model weights, adapters, inputs, derived outputs, runtime environments, and durable state cannot be conflated by a single parent data entry.

hostTools.name: google-chrome-stable
hostTools.reason: High-fidelity SVG rasterization. oksvg silently drops <filter>, <mask>, <pattern> and CSS, so a document using any of them is rendered here or refused by name — never degraded into a plausible wrong picture.
hostTools.notes: Only consulted for SVG that uses one of those four features; plain SVG keeps the pure-Go path, so this is never required (headless tenet). Discovery falls back through google-chrome, chromium, chromium-browser, chrome and headless-shell, and IMAGE_TOOLS_CHROME_BINARY overrides it. Absent, ops.rasterizeSVG returns ErrSVGFidelityUnavailable naming the features and this tool.

hostTools.name: ffmpeg
hostTools.reason: Transcode image formats Go's native imaging libraries can't fully cover (AVIF/HEIC encode, animated GIF/WebP) during deterministic format conversion
hostTools.notes: Deterministic ops use pure-Go imaging by default; ffmpeg is only consulted for the formats Go can't handle, and conversion degrades gracefully (clear error) when it is absent. Never required (headless tenet).

hostTools.name: realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan
hostTools.reason: Optional upscale/denoise backend (Real-ESRGAN ncnn-vulkan). Fetched on demand into ~/.vrooli/bin via `vrooli host install`; never auto-downloaded by default setup (headless tenet).
hostTools.notes: Data-declared url/release host tool (internal/tools/realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan). Backs the realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan provider's upscale/denoise ops.

hostTools.name: sd
hostTools.reason: Optional generative backend (stable-diffusion.cpp) for text_to_image/image_to_image. GPU-recommended; no checksum-pinnable release, so install is manual.
hostTools.notes: Capability-gated (requires GPU) in internal/tools/sd; resolves not-applicable on CPU-only hosts. Backs the stable-diffusion.cpp provider.

hostTools.name: iopaint
hostTools.reason: Optional object-removal/inpainting backend (IOPaint). Python/pip tool; surfaced but never auto-fetched.
hostTools.notes: Backs the iopaint provider's object_removal op. Install with pipx/pip (see installHint).

hostTools.name: rembg
hostTools.reason: Optional background-removal backend (rembg). Python/pip tool; surfaced but never auto-fetched.
hostTools.notes: Backs the rembg provider's background_removal/background_replace ops. Install with pipx/pip (see installHint).

hostTools.name: llama-cpp
hostTools.reason: Optional caption backend (llama.cpp multimodal runner). Built/installed manually; surfaced but never auto-fetched.
hostTools.notes: Backs the llama.cpp provider's caption op (llama-mtmd-cli/llama-cli).

hostTools.name: uv
hostTools.reason: Astral uv builds the private, lock-pinned Python venv that isolates every Python AI backend (diffusers, onnxruntime, python-sidecar). Its absolute interpreter — never the host python3 — runs the sidecars, so torch/diffusers/transformers come from internal/pydeps/requirements.lock and cannot be perturbed by other Python on the box.
hostTools.notes: Data-declared release host tool (internal/tools/uv) fetched no-sudo into ~/.vrooli/bin. On the next start image-tools builds/repairs the venv from the embedded lock; until uv is installed the Python backends report unavailable (surfaced before use), never falling back to the shared interpreter. The single Python-dependency source of truth is the lock — there is no separate pip step.
